description: BioNova is a team of three from Bursa at our first NASA Space Apps Challenge. Eymen is the brain of the team, leading the vision and every part of the build. Ömer brings design, editing, and software. Oğuz handles marketing and design. We're here to learn fast and build something real.
summary: BioNova is an offline astronaut health dashboard paired with a wearable motion sensor. On Mars a message to Earth can take up to 20 minutes, so astronauts must assess their own health. BioNova combines a live sensor with a 1-minute daily check-in (blood pressure, blood glucose, sleep, mood), shows color-coded levels, 7- and 30-day trends and a clickable 3D anatomy model, and turns each result into one clear next step: self-care, alert the crew, or call the flight surgeon. NASA DONKI space weather and NASA-STD-3001 limits drive its alerts. It runs from a single HTML file with no internet.
details:
What it does. BioNova has two screens. The astronaut screen collects health indicators from a wearable sensor (XIAO ESP32-S3 + MPU6050: motion, posture, steps, falls) and from a short daily check-in typed by the astronaut (blood pressure, blood glucose in mg/dL, sleep hours, mood). Every metric is color-coded, charted over 7 and 30 days, and linked to a body system on a clickable 3D anatomy model. A "?" card explains how to take the measurement, why it matters, and which NASA HRP hazards (radiation, isolation, distance, gravity, hostile environment) affect it. Every alert says who should act: the astronaut, the crew, or the flight surgeon. The ground-control screen receives the same data with the communication delay of the ISS, the Moon or Mars.
Benefits. Raw numbers become one clear action, so astronauts neither wait when they should act nor panic when they don't need to. The same approach fits people far from a doctor on Earth: polar stations, ships, offshore platforms and rural clinics.
How it works. The dashboard is one HTML file (JavaScript, three.js) that runs offline in any modern browser. The sensor streams over Wi-Fi WebSocket or USB. A small Python relay connects the astronaut and ground-control laptops. Health data stays in the browser.
Honest status. Live in the demo: motion, posture, steps, falls, NASA space weather. Typed in: blood pressure, glucose, sleep, mood. Simulated: heart rate, SpO2, ECG, HRV (our MAX30102 and AD8232 modules failed at the event), temperature, respiration, radiation dose and the 30-day history. The dashboard labels simulated values as "Simulation". Thresholds are general clinical ranges, not yet spaceflight-specific. BioNova is a prototype, not a medical device.
Next steps. Spaceflight-specific thresholds reviewed with flight surgeons, tests with crew data from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), a working ECG and temperature probe, and a 36 x 35 mm custom board.
